steps.title: Prepare chlorine gas sterilization
steps.instruction: Mix 100 ml household bleach (4.7 % sodium hypochlorite) with 4.5 ml 37 % HCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 435570) in a sealed container to generate chlorine gas; expose seeds to the gas overnight for surface sterilization.

steps.title: Plate and stratify sterilized seeds
steps.instruction: Plate the chlorine‑gas‑sterilized seeds on half‑strength MS agar (AM+, see Recipe 2). Stratify for 2 days at 4 °C in the dark, then place plates vertically under light for ~6 h at 21 °C. Wrap plates with aluminum foil and continue vertical growth for an additional 66 h at 21 °C.

steps.title: Prepare depletion plate
steps.instruction: In a Falcon 60 × 15 mm dish (Corning, cat 353004) pour 5 ml depletion medium (DM, see Recipe 3) and allow it to solidify. Place an 80 mm diameter cellophane foil (AA Packaging, cat 325 P) onto the agar surface and damp the foil with liquid depletion medium solution.

steps.title: Set up green‑filter microscope
steps.instruction: Place a binocular dissecting microscope in a dark room and cover its illumination with a green filter made of eight layers of green office foil.

steps.title: Select uniform seedlings
steps.instruction: Uncover the Petri dishes containing seedlings, choose seedlings with similar hypocotyl length, and exclude the longest and shortest individuals.

steps.title: Decapitate seedlings to obtain segments
steps.instruction: Using a very sharp razor blade (Gillette Wilkinson™ Sword), cut each seedling on the agar surface just below the apical hook and before the shoot‑root junction to obtain a hypocotyl segment. Prepare 6–8 segments per treatment.

steps.title: Transfer segments to depletion plate
steps.instruction: With sharp forceps, place each hypocotyl segment onto the damp cellophane foil in the depletion plate without squeezing them. Keep the plate in darkness for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Apply treatment and start scanner imaging
steps.instruction: Flip the cellophane foil onto a treatment plate containing depletion medium supplemented with either 10 µM 3‑Indoleacetic acid (IAA, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat I2886‑5G) or an ethanol mock control. Immediately place the treatment plate on a flatbed scanner, add a wet black filter paper (MACHEREY‑NAGEL, cat 409009) into the lid to improve contrast, and scan in 8‑bit grayscale at 2400 dpi every 10 min automatically using the AutoIt program (Supplemental file 1).

steps.title: Add luciferin to DR5::LUC segments
steps.instruction: For the DR5::LUC marker line, prepare 6–10 decapitated hypocotyl segments on depletion medium as above, add ~50 µl of 1 mM D‑luciferin (Duchefa Biochemie, cat L1349.0100) dissolved in 1× PBS, and immerse the segments completely for 30 min.

steps.title: Prepare treatment plates for luminescence
steps.instruction: Pour 3 ml of depletion medium (DM) containing either mock or 10 µM IAA into each well of a 12‑well tissue‑culture plate (TPP, cat 92412) and let the medium solidify (four wells can be imaged simultaneously). Note: No D‑luciferin is added to the treatment solution; the luciferin from the previous step suffices for ~5 h imaging (optional: add luciferin for longer imaging).

steps.title: Transfer segments and image luminescence
steps.instruction: Using the cellophane foil, transfer the luciferin‑treated segments onto the surface of the solidified treatment medium and remove the foil. Immediately image in a dark box with a Photometric Evolve® EMCCD camera (17 mm fixed lens/0.95 plus an additional 125 mm lens). Set EMCCD gain to 150, exposure time to 110 s, and acquire images every 2 min.

steps.title: Prepare apo‑pHusion samples
steps.instruction: Decapitate apo‑pHusion seedlings as described above. Prepare 5 ml of DM with or without 10 µM IAA. Transfer five hypocotyl segments onto the agar surface with the treatment, cut out the agar piece containing the segments with a spatula, and place it in a 2‑well Lab‑Tek™ chambered cover glass (Thermo Fisher, cat 155380) so the segments lie between the cover glass and the agar. Alternatively, pipette ~50 µl of DM with treatment onto the segments during imaging, taking extreme care not to move the sample.

steps.title: Confocal imaging of apoplastic pH
steps.instruction: Using a confocal microscope with a 20×/0.8 Plan‑Apochromat M27 objective, position each segment’s apical region via the position manager. Acquire 5 z‑sections (z‑thickness matched to the pinhole size) while simultaneously exciting GFP at 488 nm and RFP at 555 nm. Split emitted light with a short‑pass 550 nm filter (for GFP) and a long‑pass 560 nm filter (for RFP), record images at 16 bits per pixel, and repeat acquisition for all positions every 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare half‑strength MS agar (AM+)
steps.instruction: Combine half Murashige and Skoog basal salts with 1 % (w/v) sucrose, adjust pH to 5.8 with KOH, add 0.8 % (w/v) plant‑cell‑tested agar, dissolve in MilliQ water, autoclave, and pour into plates.

steps.title: Prepare depletion medium (DM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mM KCl and 1 mM MES in MilliQ water, adjust pH to 6.0 with KOH, add 1.5 % (w/v) phytagel, autoclave, and keep the liquid for use in depletion plates and treatment solutions.
